Aurora Borealis.author: W.carter
Aurora Borealis.note: Photograph of northern lights over Brastad, Sweden. Wikimedia thumbnail, otherwise unchanged. Exposure affects the apparent glow; this is not a calibrated luminance image.

Emergency Exit Sign.author: Leon Brooks
Emergency Exit Sign.note: Photograph of an illuminated exit sign. Wikimedia thumbnail, otherwise unchanged. Representative subject only; the sign's luminance was not measured.

E-Ink Reader.author: Jacek Halicki
E-Ink Reader.note: Photograph of a Kindle Paperwhite electronic-paper display. Wikimedia thumbnail, otherwise unchanged. Ambient lighting and front-light setting are not known; not a calibrated luminance image.

Laptop Screen.author: Premeditated (top left), Tom Page (top right), Maurizio Pesce (bottom left and right)
Laptop Screen.note: Photographic collage of laptops, reused unchanged from the Area dimension's local image. Representative screens only; none is documented at the listed luminance.

Neon Sign.author: Radomianin
Neon Sign.note: Photograph of the Boulevard Hotel neon sign in Miami Beach. Wikimedia thumbnail, otherwise unchanged. The photograph illustrates the source type, not its measured luminance.

White Paper in Sun.author: Brandi Redd
White Paper in Sun.note: Representative photograph of white paper, not a documented direct-sun exposure. Wikimedia thumbnail, otherwise unchanged. The source image was published under CC0 before Unsplash changed its license; no measured luminance is implied.

Traffic Signal Lens.author: Kevin Payravi
Traffic Signal Lens.note: Photograph of a red LED traffic signal in North Carolina. Wikimedia thumbnail, otherwise unchanged. Representative illuminated lens, not a luminance measurement.

Blue Sky Zenith.author: Mee2ch
Blue Sky Zenith.note: Photograph of clear blue sky near Riga. Wikimedia thumbnail, otherwise unchanged. A representative sky view; the source does not establish an exact zenith angle or calibrated luminance.

Runway Signal Lens.author: Visitor7
Runway Signal Lens.note: Photograph of runway-light hardware and its lens, not a demonstrated operating brightness. Wikimedia thumbnail, otherwise unchanged. No calibrated luminance is implied.

Theater Spotlight.author: Paul Crudgington
Theater Spotlight.note: Photograph of a performer in a theater spotlight. Shows the illuminated stage, not a close-up of the emitting lamp surface. Wikimedia thumbnail, otherwise unchanged; not a luminance measurement.

Magnesium Flare.author: Capt. John Yossarian
Magnesium Flare.note: Short-exposure photograph of burning magnesium ribbon, representative of magnesium combustion rather than a manufactured flare. Wikimedia thumbnail, otherwise unchanged; not a luminance measurement.

Core-Collapse Supernova.author: NASA, ESA, J. Hester and A. Loll (Arizona State University)
Core-Collapse Supernova.note: Hubble observational mosaic of the Crab Nebula, the remnant of SN 1054; colors encode emission from different elements. Reused unchanged from Temperature. Shows the aftermath of core collapse, not a photograph of the peak photosphere or a calibrated luminance image.

Type Ia Supernova.author: NASA/ESA, The Hubble Key Project Team and The High-Z Supernova Search Team
Type Ia Supernova.note: Hubble photograph of Type Ia supernova SN 1994D in NGC 4526; the supernova is the bright point at lower left. Reused unchanged from Energy. The photosphere is unresolved and the image does not encode the listed luminance.

Superluminous Supernova.author: Observers: D. Gerdes and S. Jouvel; inset: T. Abbott and NOAO/AURA/NSF
Superluminous Supernova.note: Observational discovery image with the supernova marked and a Blanco telescope photo inset, not a resolved stellar explosion. Downloaded unchanged from Wikimedia. The image is not calibrated to the listed effective luminance.

Magnetar Giant Flare.author: ESO/L. Calçada
Magnetar Giant Flare.note: Artist's illustration of a magnetar in Westerlund 1, reused unchanged from Magnetic Field. Not a photograph or an observed giant flare; field lines and glow are conceptual, not calibrated luminance.

Short Gamma-Ray Burst.author: University of Warwick/Mark Garlick
Short Gamma-Ray Burst.note: Artist's illustration of merging neutron stars and a kilonova, a progenitor scenario for short gamma-ray bursts. Reused unchanged from Temperature. Not a photograph of prompt gamma rays, and not calibrated luminance.

Long Gamma-Ray Burst (isotropic equivale.author: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center
Long Gamma-Ray Burst (isotropic equivale.note: NASA artist's illustration of a massive-star collapse, black hole and relativistic jet. Wikimedia thumbnail, otherwise unchanged. Not a photograph: the burst is beamed, while the dataset uses an illustrative isotropic-equivalent brightness, not a measured visible surface.
